summary: Dashboard threshold alert firing despite dashboard showing no matching series after filter change
description: Issue summary: Streamline Labs reports that a dashboard alert (percentage threshold) for 'service-error-rate' continues firing on an hourly cadence even after they applied a filter that should leave no matching series. Impact: Customer is receiving continuous pagers during business hours, causing interruption to their on-call rotation and erosion of trust in our alerting. Environment: Production analytic dashboards (console), alert configured at dashboard level, alert evaluation policy: hourly aggregate of last 5m. Occurs since filter change deployed at ~2026-03-11T22:10:00Z.
steps_to_reproduce: Open customer dashboard 'Service Health - US' in Console (customer Streamline Labs)
Apply filter: env:staging (customer previously used env:prod)
Observe that dashboard graphs show 'No data' for the selected time range and filters
Check Alerts tab: see 'High error rate (service-error-rate)' alert in firing state and recent trigger at 2026-03-12T09:00:00Z
Query alert evaluation history from alerting API: responses show non-empty timeseries and a percentage above configured threshold for same evaluation windows
observed_behavior: Dashboard panels render 'No data' for the selected filters, but the dashboard-level percentage threshold alert continues to enter 'firing' every hour. Alert evaluation API returns a series with values for the same selector despite dashboard UI showing empty results.
expected_behavior: When a dashboard query with a specific filter returns no matching series, dashboard-level alerts that rely on the same query/filter should not evaluate as firing (they should show No Data or return 'no evaluation' depending on alert policy). The alerting engine should honor the dashboard's filter semantics.
logs: Query snapshot: alert-eval used 'raw_timeseries_v2' path; dashboard visual uses 'rollup_index_v1' path
Console request id=req-94232 - customer reported via support UI at 2026-03-12T09:15:04Z
temporary_workaround: Disable the dashboard-level alert for customer to stop pagers (applied at 2026-03-12T10:05Z by Support)
Create equivalent saved query and attach alert using the rollup_index path as a short-term step (works while investigation ongoing)
business_impact: Customer experiencing repeated on-call pages and has asked for an incident review. This is affecting one enterprise customer with potential churn risk if not resolved within 48 hours.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:15 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reported ~20 pagers since midnight local. They changed dashboard filters yesterday; alert started firing after that. Asked for immediate mute option.

2026-03-12 10:40 - Liam Patel (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Dashboard UI shows no data; alert evaluation returns values when run against raw_timeseries_v2 backend. Suspect mismatch between query pipelines (rollup vs raw) and a stale tag mapping cache.

2026-03-12 13:05 - Maria Ortiz (Platform): Found cache invalidation event failed at 2026-03-11T22:08Z during rollup deploy. Rollup index is missing the 'env:staging' tag mapping for this metric; alert path falls back to raw which still has previous tag mapping -> non-empty series.

2026-03-13 08:23 - Liam Patel (SRE): Hotfix applied: restarted rollup-indexer and invalidated metric-tag cache for customer namespace. Monitored for two evaluation windows; no new alerts observed while dashboard shows no data. Reopening for follow-up and root cause fix.
2026-03-14 11:40 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer confirmed pager volume stopped after hotfix. They request timeline and permanent fix before we close ticket.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Alert evaluator uses a different query planner than dashboard panels; it landed on raw_timeseries path which retained older tag values.
Hypothesis 2: Cache invalidation for rollup index failed during last rollout, leaving rollup index blind to env:staging tag causing dashboard to return no data while raw still returns metrics.

Evidence: Deployment logs show a failed cache purge call at 2026-03-11T22:08:07Z (error 502 from cache-service). Rollup index rebuild partial. Alert evaluator logs show fallback to raw path when rollup response is inconsistent.
Repro script: reproduced locally by simulating partial rollup index state; alerts evaluated against raw path produce non-empty series while dashboard returns empty.
resolution_notes: Hotfix: restarted rollup-indexer and forced cache invalidation for Streamline Labs namespace at 2026-03-13T08:23Z. Verified alert evaluations aligned with dashboard queries for three consecutive evaluation windows.
Root cause: failed cache purge during rollup deployment caused divergence between rollup index and raw_timeseries tag mappings; alert evaluator chose raw path and produced false positives.

Permanent fix planned: ensure alerting evaluator uses unified query pipeline that prefers rollup_index and respects dashboard filter semantics; add guard to treat 'no series' as 'no data' instead of evaluating default fallback. Patch planned in PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12245.

Follow-ups: add regression tests for dashboard/alert parity, improve deployment runbook to ensure cache purge retries, and add an automated check that validates rollup vs raw tag mapping post-deploy. Assigned to Platform team for 2-week sprint (owner: Maria Ortiz).
